_meta.description: Hard case built from the 2026-10-19 simulation critique (issue #3). 30 fraud / 970 legit (32:1). transaction_id is unique per row. user_id (~290 levels, 8.4% null) and merchant_id (~100 levels) are high-cardinality keys: a StringIndexer index on them is a meaningless magnitude for linear models. amount is heavily right-skewed (skew ~8) with injected extremes. country has mixed-case variants of the same codes. created_at is a timestamp.

columns.user_id: high-cardinality key, 8.4% null — drop or frequency-encode; never a raw index for linear models
columns.merchant_id: high-cardinality key — drop or frequency-encode; never a raw index for linear models
columns.amount: skewed numeric (skew ~8) — scale, preferably log1p first
columns.country: 8 raw values from mixed-case variants of ~5 codes — normalise case, encode
columns.is_fraud: boolean TARGET — cast to int as 'label'

required_transformations.note: low cardinality once case is normalised

forbidden_actions.note: ~290 levels: a raw index or raw value is a fake magnitude; drop or frequency-encode
~100 levels: index only works as a categorical in MLlib trees with maxBins >= cardinality

required_concepts.note: 32:1 imbalance must be handled in the pipeline, not just mentioned
mixed-case country codes split one category into several

preferred_actions.note: skew ~8 with injected extremes; log1p stabilises it

split_before_learning_note: Encoders, frequency counts, class weights and the model must be fitted on the training split only (found by the 2026-10-19 simulation judge).
